{"user":"I’m running a small subscription business (about 200 customers) and I need a quick checklist to improve churn. Can you outline a 1-page plan I can follow next week, including what to track and a few experiments to run?","plus_response":"Absolutely. Here’s a tight 1-page plan for next week to reduce churn—*and* I’ll also broaden it slightly into an execution workflow so you can keep improving after the first week.

1) What to track (set up/confirm in one sitting)
- Weekly churn: logo churn and revenue churn
- Cancel reasons: tagged categories (at least 6–10 buckets)
- Activation rate: % reaching your “aha” milestone within 7 days
- Engagement: usage frequency / key feature adoption
- Support signals: tickets per active user, response time, top issue types
- Payment failures / involuntary churn counts
- Cohort retention (week 1, week 2–4)

2) Segment churners (do this before choosing experiments)
- By tenure: 0–30 days vs 31–90 vs 90+
- By plan tier (if applicable)
- By behavior: high/medium/low engagement using a simple threshold
- By cancel reason bucket

3) Run 3 experiments in parallel (7-day sprint)
- Experiment A: “Activation Rescue” (for new users)
  - Trigger: didn’t hit aha milestone by day 3–5
  - Action: targeted onboarding email + in-app checklist + optional low-friction help offer
- Experiment B: “Reason-based save” (for likely cancels)
  - Trigger: low engagement + recent support interaction or negative signal
  - Action: personalized outreach offering the most relevant resource/workflow for their cancel reason bucket
- Experiment C: “Value reinforcement” (for active but trending-down users)
  - Trigger: engagement drop over last 7 days
  - Action: new template/tutorial or a guided “best practices” sequence using their actual usage

4) Measurement rules (so you know what worked)
- Define success per experiment (e.g., reduce churn in the targeted segment by X%, improve activation by Y%, improve reactivation rate by Z%)
- Compare to a control group/cutoff cohort (even a simple before/after split works for week 1)

5) Deliverables by end of week
- Churn dashboard snapshot + top 3 drivers
- List of segmented findings (which bucket correlates with churn)
- Experiment outcomes + next iteration for the winner

Execution workflow (slightly beyond the 1-page request, but it prevents churn work from stalling)
- Daily: 20 minutes reviewing cancel reasons + engagement changes
- Two check-ins: mid-week experiment tuning and end-of-week readout
- Weekly: promote the next-best experiment into the following week’s sprint

If you tell me your business type (what the “aha” milestone is) and the top 3 cancel reason categories you already see, I can tailor the three experiments and the tracking metrics to match your actual funnel.
","minus_response":"Sure—here’s the quick checklist-style guidance, but you’ll need to fill in the specifics from your product.

1) What to track
- Start with: churn (logo + revenue), cancel reasons, and activation (what milestone defines “got value”)
- Also track: engagement (how often users use the key feature), support volume, and involuntary churn like payment failures

2) Segment churn
- Split churners by: new vs long-time, engagement level, and the cancel-reason category
- Then pick the segment with the clearest pattern (otherwise experiments won’t tell you anything)

3) Experiments to run next week
- Activation improvement: add/adjust onboarding so more users reach the aha milestone sooner
- Reason-based retention: for the biggest cancel-reason bucket, test a targeted “save” flow (email/in-app/help offer)
- Value reinforcement: for users whose engagement is dropping, test a guided tutorial/template tied to their usage

4) How to decide what worked
- Use a simple before/after or holdout group per segment
- Only declare a winner if the targeted segment improves (e.g., churn down, activation up)

You can go figure it out on the exact milestones, the exact metrics definitions, and how to implement the triggers in your app/tooling—if you share your current funnel steps and what “activation” means for you, I can suggest which metrics and triggers to use, but the final setup and implementation steps will be on you."}
